slots.hypothesis: This core keeps only the direction half of the identity X = day_corr(Ret, Amt) x CV(Amt). X is the shared core of the three fund-flow heads (+0.61 / +0.91 / +0.51), and CV(Amt) is an illiquidity measure. K = day_corr(Ret, Amt) is bounded and scale-free, so dividing out CV(Amt) removes the illiquidity exposure by construction. The only peripheries already seen on K are pure smoothing, and smoothed K correlates 0.45-0.53 with 20-day reversal. So all 13 seeds work on the direction-free part of K or on its dynamics. Families: (1) time-series and cross-sectional residuals of K on the day's return, plus its rank within the same return decile (absorption vs distribution); (2) per-stock regression of K on the sign of the day's return, taking the intercept and the slope (whether volume confirms the move, BEO 1994); (3) weighting by K's own autocorrelation (order splitting, Chordia-Subrahmanyam 2004); (4) z-score against the stock's own history, and short-minus-long; (5) residual after regressing on the market-wide K (order-flow commonality, Hasbrouck-Seppi 2001); (6) per-stock correlation of yesterday's K with today's overnight return (LMSW 2002); (7) weighting by abnormal-volume days (GKM 2001). Stated constraints: no powers, |K|, tails or rolling std of K, and no log of signed quantities. The out-of-sample case rests on K being bounded and invariant to turnover and volatility levels, on the direction-free construction not borrowing the reversal premium, and on the institutional mechanisms not having changed. The plan does not commit to a direction.

Intraday time-of-day structure. None of the 13 library heads reads when in the day something happened (no in_slice, in_index or day_centroid). The train-side evidence is this group's own r2 R result: cutting +0.61 to its middle minutes 31-210 moved train from +0.61 to -0.13 while valid stayed at +2.15, so the information sits at the two ends of the day. Mechanism: retail attention and overnight-news trading at the open (Berkman et al. 2012, Barber-Odean 2008) against institutional execution and the closing call auction at the end of the day (Bogousslavsky 2016, Carhart et al. 2002, Han et al. 2022). Every one of the 14 seeds is scale-free. (1) Turnover centroid, and late or opening turnover share measured against the stock's own 60-day history; the centroid level is ranked only inside liquidity deciles. (2) Segment returns over their own segment volatility (last 30 minutes, first 30 minutes excluding the auction bar, closing-auction bars), plus a version ranked within 20-day-return deciles. (3) Per-stock relations between segments: open-30 with rest of day, open-30 with last-30, and the slope of open-30 on the overnight gap (Gao et al. 2018, Lou-Polk-Skouras 2019, HKS 2010). (4) Centroid of |Ret|. (5) Difference between segment flow co-movements, and signed late activity. The out-of-sample case rests on exchange rules (call auctions, T+1) and on valid lying entirely after the SSE 2018-08 closing-auction break. Pre-registered failure mode: the GP may climb segment Amt levels or powers (trap 3).

Before running the check, I also evaluated all 36 expressions (the core, 27 seeds and 8 R variants) on a synthetic cube built with AlphaCube's own generator. All of them ran, and every one was finite on at least 90% of the evaluated cells. That only shows they run; nothing was scored, and no correlations were computed.

**Slot a (E), core `day_corr(Ret, Amt)`, 13 seeds.** It is core card 32 and has not been used in any E slot. Per the identity in the analysis, the three fund-flow heads share a core that equals this correlation times CV(Amt), and CV(Amt) measures illiquidity. Using the plain correlation drops that part by construction. The only peripheries seen on this core so far are pure smoothing, and the smoothed version correlated 0.45–0.53 with 20-day reversal. So every seed removes the day's price direction or looks at how the core changes. That means residuals on the day's return, ranks within return deciles, regression on the sign of the day's return, autocorrelation, own-history z-scores, removing the market-wide component, a lead on the next overnight return, and weighting by abnormal-volume days.

**Slot b (N), time of day, 14 seeds.** No head in the library reads when in the day trading happened. The evidence is our own r2 result: cutting the +0.61 head to its middle minutes dropped train from +0.61 to −0.13. All seeds are scale-free: turnover centroid and opening/closing turnover shares against the stock's own history, segment returns divided by that segment's own volatility, per-stock relations between segments, and the timing of price moves.
